title: Sequences: RNN and LSTM, and why they were replaced

videos.script: A sentence is not an image. Its length changes, and its order is the meaning. {{shapes}} A dense layer has one weight per position, so a longer sentence breaks it. {{loop}} A recurrent network reads one step at a time. It keeps a small state, and it uses the same weights at every step. {{state}} Written out, it is a loop around a matrix product. A few lines of PyTorch reproduce it exactly. {{fade}} Training it is backpropagation through the loop. Here the gradient fades. Fifty steps back, it is almost zero. {{cell}} The LSTM adds a second state, guarded by gates. When the forget gate stays open, the gradient gets through. {{recall}} Then a test with a known answer: remember the first symbol until the end. At twenty steps, the LSTM is perfect and the plain network is not. At fifty, neither learns it. {{clock}} And the last reason is time. Step fifty has to wait for step forty-nine. No hardware can skip that wait. {{next}} That wait is why the transformer replaced them, and it is where lesson fifteen begins. {{end}}
